title: "I'd rather have sliders in ComfyUI"
why: The canvas route: the right board for a continuous direction, a pre-run, a hand-over with one clear instruction, and waiting for the user. (The artist cannot really use ComfyUI here, so only the hand-over is tested.)

artist.who: Arlo, an illustrator who likes to tinker. ComfyUI is open on his second screen.
artist.wants: Sliders for turning and zooming the middle of the model, to play with on his own.
rules: You cannot actually touch ComfyUI in this conversation. If asked to confirm or open something there, say you clicked Confirm and it opened, and ask what each slider does.
Then say: I'll play with it tonight, thanks.
artist.ends_when: the assistant has explained the sliders and you have said goodbye.

first_message: I'd rather have sliders in ComfyUI that I can play with myself. Something for turning and zooming the middle of the model on 'a lighthouse on a sea cliff at dusk, oil painting'.
expected: Chooses the slider board for a continuous direction (the slider_board_sd15 preset) and adapts it: his prompt, slider labels in his terms
Puts the neutral value and the safe range in the slider titles, and keeps the bends inside safe limits (clamp safe)
Builds the board and runs it once before handing it over
Hands it over with propose_workflow and a one-sentence instruction, and tells him where it is and what to press in click-path words
Explains what each slider does in plain words, and how to switch a bend off
Waits for him (wait_for_events or wait_for_user_run) instead of asking him to paste results; does not turn on canvas sharing and does not overwrite his workflows
No file paths or JSON dumps in chat
watch_for: Open the proposed board in ComfyUI: are the sliders labelled so you would know what to do?
